quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can you reduce head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. It is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike, since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Learn the controls and gear pattern before you ride. Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: What kind of soles should motorcycle riding shoes have?
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position your motorcycle to be seen clearly. Keep space around your bike to react to danger.

questions.question: Why should you keep a safe distance behind other vehicles?

options.text: To have time and space to spot and avoid hazards.
So traffic counters count you correctly.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To have time and space to spot and avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: A safe distance gives you room to stop or steer away if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see hazards on the road like potholes.

questions.question: What material should protective jackets and pants be made from?
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs. Leather clothing provides the best protection.

questions.question: What road sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: You do not need to check your blind spot if you use mirrors.
Mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Assume drivers will respond to your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always check your blind spot by turning your head and looking over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It contains details about how to operate it and maintain it.

questions.question: Who is most likely to have a crash?

options.text: Those who completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Beginning riders who are untrained and unfamiliar with their motorcycle are most likely to crash.

questions.question: In general, the body gets rid of almost ______ per hour.
questions.explanation: On average, your body can eliminate the alcohol from about one drink per hour.

questions.question: A way to lower the risk of a crash is to:

options.text: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
Ride in parts of the lane where others cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Signal your turns and stops. Use your brake light. Position yourself well in your lane. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When riding on a bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Relax, maintain steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is normal and not dangerous. Stay calm and ride straight at a steady speed. Do not zigzag to fight the weave, as this is dangerous and can force you out of your lane.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always look ahead and expect possible dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because they are rare.
Look ahead but try not to look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and expect possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Always look far ahead of your motorcycle to spot hazards early. This gives you time to react before you reach them.

questions.question: It is a good idea to wear reflective clothing:
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright clothing whenever you ride. Crashes happen in daylight and at night. It is best to wear highly visible clothing at all times.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after one drink before riding:

options.text: Means you cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Means your riding skills will not be affected.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not fully remove alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not fully remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. But the time needed varies from person to person. The safest choice is to never ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: Your motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers see that you are braking.

questions.question: A simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see is to:

options.text: Ride with a large flag attached to its frame.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.explanation: Make yourself easier to see by wearing bright, reflective clothing. Ride with your headlight on at all times. Use your turn signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: Which helmet type is the safest?
questions.explanation: A full-face helmet is the safest because it protects your face and chin in a crash. Half-shell and three-quarter-shell helmets do not protect your face.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: What should an approved helmet allow?

options.text: You to see clearly to the sides for safe riding.
You to ride without a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: You to see clearly to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet will not limit your vision. You will be able to see everything you need to see for safe riding.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair your riding?

options.text: At about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired well before reaching the legal blood alcohol limit. It is never safe to drink before riding.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing helps other drivers see you in all conditions. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothing whenever you ride.

questions.question: Why should you rise off your seat when approaching a bump or pothole?

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the impact.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact force. This reduces the shock and helps keep you from being thrown off the motorcycle.
